links.outcome: Real-world positive predictive value of AI LVO detection across the tele-stroke population
links.effect: Among transferred patients, NCCT high-probability predictions had 66% (41/62) EVT and CTA 67% (36/54). Screening-log estimates across all scans suggested modest-to-weak real-world PPV.
links.quote: These estimations suggested a modest-to-weak real-world performance and support the concept that AI-based LVO detection tools are most appropriately applied in clinically pre-selected populations with moderate-to-high suspicion of LVO.

links.outcome: Time from local centre arrival to transfer request before vs after AI
links.effect: CE-marked tool reported 87.2%/87.7% NCCT sensitivity/specificity, but door-to-transfer request was unchanged (59 vs 61 min; adjusted median difference −2.40; 95% CI −6.16 to 4.48).
links.quote: Artificial intelligence implementation was not associated with a shorter time to transfer decision.

links.outcome: Transfer decision and treatment times with clinician-accessible AI versus usual tele-stroke care
links.effect: Arrival-to-transfer request: −2.40 min (95% CI, −6.16 to 4.48); imaging-to-request: −7.16 min (95% CI, −13.02 to −1.85); arrival-to-puncture: −31.28 min (95% CI, −60.89 to −13.74). Increased CTA availability limited AI-specific attribution.
links.quote: Time from arrival at the local-SC to EMS transfer request did not differ significantly between the pre- and post-implementation cohorts (59 [43–88] vs 61 [46–99] min; adjusted median difference: −2.40; 95% CI, −6.16 to 4.48) ( Figure 2A ).

links.outcome: 90-day functional outcomes and transfer-related complications versus standard care
links.effect: 90-day mRS: median 2 [IQR 1–4] in both groups; aOR = 1.01; 95% CI, 0.59–1.71. No transfer-related complications were reported in either group.
links.quote: At 90-day follow-up, the distribution of mRS scores was similar between cohorts (median 2 [IQR 1–4] in both groups; aOR = 1.01; 95% CI, 0.59–1.71) ( Table S7 ).

links.effect: Broad application yielded a 66% positive predictive value, suggesting the tool is best used in clinically pre-selected populations.
links.quote: These estimations suggested a modest-to-weak real-world performance and support the concept that AI-based LVO detection tools are most appropriately applied in clinically pre-selected populations with moderate-to-high suspicion of LVO.

links.effect: AI implementation was not associated with a shorter time to transfer decision, demonstrating a lack of expected clinical benefit.
links.quote: Artificial intelligence implementation was not associated with a shorter time to transfer decision.

links.effect: Implementing the AI-based triage tool in the network workflow did not shorten transfer decision times.
links.quote: In our hub-and-spoke stroke network, implementing an AI-based triage tool did not shorten transfer decision times.

screen.reason: Prospective quasi-experimental study of the clinical implementation of an AI stroke imaging tool (Methinks Stroke Suite) assessing clinical and workflow outcomes.
